headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap: Open Interpreter can modify the local machine while langchain4j can ingest trusted content, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter reads clipboard/files and can execute code from user-visible content; langchain4j is a framework that can ingest external text into LLM workflows. A shared filesystem/clipboard bridge exists, so attacker-controlled content from one side can be treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented for this pair.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange text through clipboard or shared files
IF langchain4j prompts are built from Open Interpreter output without sanitization
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Use separate directories for each agent
Wrap all inter-agent text in inert quoting
Add a prompt-injection filter before langchain4j ingestion
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every transferred artifact

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter has broad filesystem read/write and broad network egress, while langchain4j is a framework that can route content to model providers. If both touch the same local files, sensitive data can flow from the machine into model prompts or outputs without a dedicated isolation boundary. The pairwise leakage path is supported by both profiles, though not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF both agents access the same local directory
IF Open Interpreter reads sensitive files that langchain4j later includes in prompts or logs
IF model-provider calls are enabled for Open Interpreter or downstream consumers
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate workspaces
Remove secrets from shared directories before use
Disable network access for any run handling sensitive files
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter can write the filesystem and modify git state; langchain4j can participate in workflows that consume or emit files, but its write surface is not explicitly listed. Because the pair shares filesystem-based state via Open Interpreter and the other agent may read/write through its host application, uncertainty about langchain4j's write path escalates rather than lowers severity.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF langchain4j writes artifacts that Open Interpreter also edits
IF git state is mutated without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git locks or a single-writer policy
Review diffs before commit
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared files

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can take actions on the local machine, and langchain4j can generate or route content that may be treated as authoritative in a support workflow. If Open Interpreter consumes langchain4j output without verification, a mistaken answer can cascade into file edits, shell commands, or commits. The blast radius is larger than a single document, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter executes commands derived from langchain4j output
IF langchain4j output is not independently verified before action
IF the workflow allows auto-run or equivalent confirmation bypass
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Disable auto-run modes
Add a verification step for all generated facts
Limit Open Interpreter to read-only tasks
requires-engineering: separate generation from execution with a policy gate

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter touches anything reachable on the local machine and can send content to configured model providers; langchain4j is a framework that may also route data to external providers. If regulated data is present locally, residency and retention obligations can diverge across the two paths. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is present on the local machine
IF either agent forwards that data to a third-party model provider
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the two processing paths
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders
Use approved providers only
Delete temporary artifacts after each run
Document retention settings for both agents
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and audit logs
